claude.sample_unit: pediatric ICU patients (Experiment A); 63,203 adult ICU patients in Experiment B

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration recovery after target-domain retraining on local data
links.effect: RF ROC-AUC fell from 0.940 to 0.725 in younger children; retraining recovered 0.867; ECE rose from ≤0.010 to 0.142 and was restored below 0.01. Retraining on 5% (~180 patients) recovered most of the gap.
links.quote: Random Forest ROC-AUC fell from 0.940 (95% CI 0.912-0.968) on older children to 0.725 (0.703-0.746) on younger children, and target-domain retraining recovered 0.867 (0.842-0.890); ECE rose from ≤0.010 to 0.142 and was restored below 0.01.

links.outcome: Model performance when transferred from adult/older-child cohorts to a new younger population
links.effect: Discrimination fell from 0.940 to 0.725 in younger children; adult-ICU models became severely miscalibrated (ECE up to 0.285); neonates AUC 0.587 (ECE 0.249).
links.quote: Vital-sign-based mortality models trained on older children or directly observed adult-ICU data lose discrimination and become severely miscalibrated when applied to younger children, with neonates worst affected.

links.outcome: Dataset shift between development and deployment populations degrading performance
links.effect: Adult vs pediatric vitals showed large shifts (heart-rate d=+2.75, respiratory-rate d=+3.06) with ECE rising to 0.285 and discrimination loss in younger children.
links.quote: In the directly observed adult-ICU Experiment B the domain shift was confirmed with directly observed vitals (heart-rate Cohen's d=+2.75, respiratory-rate d=+3.06) and manifested mainly as severe miscalibration (ECE rising to 0.285) with a smaller, model-dependent discrimination change, again removed by target-domain retraining.

links.outcome: Performance across age-band subgroups hidden by aggregate metrics
links.effect: Performance fell monotonically with age, from 0.992 in preschool children to 0.587 in neonates (ECE 0.249).
links.quote: Performance fell monotonically with age, from 0.992 in preschool children to 0.587 in neonates (ECE 0.249).

links.outcome: Model performance when applied outside validated population
links.effect: Models trained on adults or older children lost discrimination and were miscalibrated in younger children, worst in neonates.
links.quote: Vital-sign-based mortality models trained on older children or directly observed adult-ICU data lose discrimination and become severely miscalibrated when applied to younger children, with neonates worst affected.

screen.practice: target-domain retraining and recalibration before pediatric deployment
screen.reason: Evaluates transfer gap and compares deployment adaptation strategies (target-domain retraining vs recalibration-only updating) when transferring adult ICU models to pediatric cohorts.
